formalized_procedure.note: Verbatim: "Compute e[:,u] for samples in completed runs and then every m[s,j,q,b]; output the ordered-pair run-margin table." e=(Lsrc-Lcar)/(Lsrc+Lcar), with zero-denominator e=0; m is the normalized within-run sum, with zero-denominator m=0.

Verbatim: "For each q with at least n_run completed runs, compute a and R; output observed pair orientations and their across-run replication." Two readings exist for "fraction of runs whose nonzero margin has the sign of a": denominator all completed runs, or only nonzero-margin runs. The patch binds the first reading explicitly; the S5 blocking result holds under either because a run-label permutation preserves both numerator and denominator.

Verbatim: "Apply P_perm joint circular run-block permutations within q and compute R0 and G; output the excess-replicated dominance tensor while preserving candidate coupling and the fixed path." R0 aggregation is not specified in the candidate; the natural Monte Carlo mean is patched in. More importantly, any bijective whole-run permutation leaves the multiset of m values invariant, so a, R, and every R^(p) are identical.

Verbatim: "Compute S[:,q_t]; if all scores tie or q_t lacks n_run completed runs, output the identity candidate order, otherwise output the stable descending S order." N=1 divides by zero. The phrase "identity candidate order" also has two readings downstream: bypass reassignment, or use original identifiers as the target order for sorted values. The patch adds N<2 handling and an explicit bypass flag.

Verbatim: "Stable-sort the original Lsrc[:,t] values and assign them by the M3 candidate order to form Ltilde[:,t]; output exactly the original multiset under a possibly different candidate labeling." Under the literal target-order reading, a tie sends descending values to original identifiers and is not an identity assignment unless Lsrc already happens to be sorted by identifier. The patch makes fallback bypass sorting.

execution.script:
from itertools import permutations
from statistics import median
CANDS = ("A", "B", "C")
onset_runs = [[[0.2, 0.9, -0.1]], [[0.1, 0.8, -0.2]], [[0.0, 0.7, -0.3]]]
blank_runs = [
    [[0.9, 0.0, -0.4], [0.9, 0.0, -0.4]],
    [[0.9, 0.0, -0.4], [0.9, 0.0, -0.4]],
    [[0.9, 0.0, -0.4], [0.9, 0.0, -0.4]],
]
def margin(run, s, j):
    diffs = [row[s] - row[j] for row in run]
    den = sum(abs(x) for x in diffs)
    return 0.0 if den == 0 else sum(diffs) / den
def pair_stats(runs, s, j):
    ms = [margin(run, s, j) for run in runs]
    a = median(ms)
    sign_a = (a > 0) - (a < 0)
    r = sum(m != 0 and ((m > 0) - (m < 0)) == sign_a for m in ms) / len(ms)
    return ms, a, r
obs = {(s,j): pair_stats(onset_runs,s,j) for s in range(3) for j in range(3) if s != j}
perm_rs = {key: [] for key in obs}
for perm in permutations(range(len(onset_runs))):
    permuted = [onset_runs[k] for k in perm]
    for key in obs:
        perm_rs[key].append(pair_stats(permuted, *key)[2])
g = {}
for key, (_, a, r) in obs.items():
    r0 = sum(perm_rs[key]) / len(perm_rs[key])
    g[key] = a * max(0.0, r-r0)
scores = [sum(g[s,j] for j in range(3) if j != s)/2 for s in range(3)]
global_sum = [sum(row[s] for run in onset_runs+blank_runs for row in run) for s in range(3)]
naive_order = sorted(range(3), key=lambda s: (-global_sum[s], s))
current_lsrc = [0.9,0.4,0.2]
sorted_values = sorted(current_lsrc, reverse=True)
naive_out = [None]*3
for rank,s in enumerate(naive_order): naive_out[s] = sorted_values[rank]
mechanism_identity = current_lsrc[:]
perturbed_lsrc = [0.2,0.9,0.4]
literal_tie_out = sorted(perturbed_lsrc, reverse=True)
print("onset_pair_margins_A_vs_B=", obs[0,1][0])
print("onset_pair_margins_B_vs_A=", obs[1,0][0])
print("observed_R_B_vs_A=", obs[1,0][2])
print("unique_permuted_R_B_vs_A=", sorted(set(perm_rs[1,0])))
print("R0_B_vs_A=", sum(perm_rs[1,0])/len(perm_rs[1,0]))
print("G_B_vs_A=", g[1,0])
print("all_G_zero=", all(x == 0 for x in g.values()))
print("scores_A_B_C=", scores)
print("global_evidence_A_B_C=", global_sum)
print("naive_order=", [CANDS[i] for i in naive_order])
print("naive_output=", naive_out)
print("mechanism_identity_output=", mechanism_identity)
print("naive_equals_mechanism=", naive_out == mechanism_identity)
print("perturbed_input=", perturbed_lsrc)
print("literal_steps_6_7_tie_output=", literal_tie_out)
print("literal_tie_is_identity=", literal_tie_out == perturbed_lsrc)

final_candidate.core_mechanism: The shared object is a regime-replicated dominance tensor G[s,j,q] computed causally before update t for each ordered candidate pair (s,j) and observed hit-transition regime q. Let h_t be the frozen M1/M2 GADEN hit indicator and q_t=(h_{t-1},h_t), giving the four structural regimes blank, onset, persistence, and exit without a new threshold; let Lsrc[s,t] and Lcar[s,t] be the existing nonnegative source and carrier likelihood fields, and define bounded source-over-carrier evidence e[s,t]=(Lsrc[s,t]-Lcar[s,t])/(Lsrc[s,t]+Lcar[s,t]), with e=0 when the denominator is zero. For every maximal completed run b of regime q strictly before t, compute the pairwise run margin m[s,j,q,b]=sum_{u in b}(e[s,u]-e[j,u])/sum_{u in b}|e[s,u]-e[j,u]|, set to zero only when its denominator is zero, and let a[s,j,q] be the median run margin. With n_run=3 as the preregistered minimum number of completed runs, chosen because it is the smallest count that permits one run to be held out while two establish an orientation, define R[s,j,q] as the fraction of runs whose nonzero margin has the sign of a[s,j,q]; regimes with fewer runs contribute zero. Estimate the spurious-replication level R0[s,j,q] by P_perm=199 joint circular run-block permutations within q, the smallest odd count giving two-sided Monte Carlo resolution at most 0.01, where the same permutation is applied to every candidate field so candidate coupling and temporal blocks survive but observation-to-field alignment is broken. Set G[s,j,q]=a[s,j,q] max(0,R[s,j,q]-R0[s,j,q]) and the current-regime score S[s,q_t]=(|S|-1)^{-1} sum_{j!=s}G[s,j,q_t]; this is not covariance whitening, robust M-estimation, or change detection because the load-bearing artifact is candidate-pair orientation that exceeds a coupled block null. At update t, sort the existing values {Lsrc[s,t]} and assign them in descending order to candidates sorted by S[s,q_t], retaining the original candidate order for ties; this order transport defines Ltilde[s,t], exactly preserves the likelihood-value multiset, and becomes the sole M3 output consumed by the unchanged Bayesian accumulator and myopic action selector. The diagnostic leg evaluates the same G tensor with sequestered GADEN source identities only after all causal outputs are frozen, and M3 defaults to the identity assignment whenever all current-regime scores tie, providing a truth-blind activation boundary rather than a tuned posterior multiplier. Here R is the number of all completed runs with a nonzero margin whose sign equals sign(a), divided by the total completed-run count; for permutation p compute R^(p) by the same rule and define R0=P_perm^{-1} sum_p R^(p).

Block randomization is a standard diagnostic tool, but this instance is not solved by an iid permutation test because all candidate fields share one adaptively chosen UAV path and turbulent blocks; the contribution uses a joint trajectory-preserving null to drive a candidate-label likelihood assignment, not merely a p-value.
